answer: A sparrow crosses a river on one wing only once, and so should an identity. Dual-chain bonded identity locks a stake on two independent chains, with fraud proof on either chain slashing both deposits. An attacker must fund and risk capital in two ecosystems, coordinate keys and timing across both, and still lose everything if one proof lands. The ripple effect is the point: one exposure destroys the whole position, not just a single copy. The limit is real: honest users pay double lock-up and fees, small holders are priced out, and an outage on either chain can freeze a legitimate identity.
